yang_pipeline_overview.trigger_mechanism: The yang pipeline is triggered by an S3 event on the opal-data-portal-v2 bucket. The PM team uploads a manifest.json to the uploads/ prefix, which invokes the yang-pipeline-trigger Lambda. The manifest lists which file types are present in this run (data_pkl, model_pkl, attribution_excel, peer_excel, cma_excel, saa_excel). Only the generator Lambdas for present file types are executed.

step_functions_execution_order.step: Reads manifest.json from uploads/ to determine which file types are present.
Moves uploaded files to processed/{execution_id}/ prefix.
Retrieves metadata from previous pipeline run for diff/change detection.

Writes json/latest/{file_type}.json pointer files (one per file type present). Each pointer contains: file_type, pattern, frequency, latest_version, data_as_of, s3_key, original_filename, uploaded_at, pipeline_execution_id.
If data_pkl is present: runs yang-ingest-dynamodb FIRST (before all generator Lambdas). This populates the opal-portal-market-data DynamoDB table before any downstream consumers read it.

branch.name: cma_excel branch
branch.lambda: yang-generate-cma (OUT OF SCOPE — owned by DS_MarketIntelligence)

step_functions_execution_order.step: Reads all json/latest/{file_type}.json files and aggregates them into a single json/latest/manifest.json. This is the unified version pointer the portal reads to know which data is current. Final step before cleanup.
Scans json/ prefix for files modified in last 10 minutes. Captures S3 version IDs for rollback. Writes to data-refresh/archive/{execution_id}/outputs-manifest.json.
Invalidates CloudFront distribution cache after manifest generation.

yang_pipeline_overview.data_flow: yang-pipeline Lambda → writes JSON to s3://opal-data-portal-v2/json/{category}/ → opal-portal-data-proxy Lambda fetches and serves via portal-proxy API → CloudFront CDN → portal client (React)

page.name: FactorTilts
page.note: FactorTilts uses a tiered loading architecture. All three tiers are produced by the same single Lambda (yang-generate-factor-tilts) in one execution, written to three separate S3 keys. The portal fetches them lazily on demand to control payload size.

page.name: Macroeconomics
page.note: Macroeconomics is served by TWO separate Yang Lambdas: yang-generate-macro (main heatmap + VIX file) and yang-generate-macro-timeseries (per-indicator drill-down files, fetched on demand). A third Lambda (yang-generate-volatility) is a separate, independent component that produces the VolatilityTab data with FRED API (not the data_pkl). The YieldCurveTab data comes from a separate yield-curve endpoint and is outside the Yang pipeline.

source.input_data: data_pkl: benchmarks/data_{YYYYMMDD}_{version}.pkl - 73+ macroeconomic indicator time series indexed by Bloomberg ticker - Grouped into 10 categories: Leading, Lagging, Financial Condition, Inflation, Labor Market, Consumer, Housing, Investor Sentiment, Treasury Yields, Credit Spread, Market Indicator, Currency

source.input_data: data_pkl: benchmarks/data_{YYYYMMDD}_{version}.pkl - VIX time series data (derived from macro indicator subset in PKL) NOTE: This is distinct from yang-generate-volatility. The yang-generate-macro Lambda writes a separate VIX-specific JSON as a convenience output alongside macro_data.json.

note.title: Alpha factor attribution join: permid vs company_name
note.description:
The yang-generate-holdings-attribution Lambda joins attribution Excel data to holdings using DynamoDB etf-classifications (keyed by ticker). Historical root cause: an earlier version of this Lambda attempted to join attribution rows by company_name (display string), which produced silent mismatches when name spellings differed between the Excel source and the portfolio holdings data (e.g., whitespace, abbreviation, casing differences). The fix was to use ticker as the canonical join key, backed by the etf-classifications DynamoDB table.
Current risk: if the attribution Excel contains tickers not present in DynamoDB etf-classifications, those rows will fail to classify and be dropped from the output. The etf-classifications table must be kept current with any new ETF positions added to the model portfolios.

note.title: Attribution effects are null: policyWeight and benchmarkReturn not populated
note.description:
Both Positioning/utils/buildAttributionData.ts and Attribution/utils/buildAttributionData.ts (separate copies with identical logic) hard-code policyWeight as null and benchmarkReturn as null. As a result, allocationEffect, selectionEffect, and interactionEffect all compute as null throughout the attribution display.
This is a data contract gap, not a frontend bug. Resolution requires: 1. Defining the policy portfolio data source (likely benchmark_holdings from model_pkl or a dedicated policy portfolio file) 2. Defining the benchmark return mapping (likely from yang-generate-benchmark-returns output) 3. Updating buildAttributionData.ts in both pages to read these sources
This is the single most impactful open data gap in the PortfolioAnalytics pod.

note.title: Holdings attribution periods: QTD and YTD only
note.description: yang-generate-holdings-attribution currently generates attribution data for QTD and YTD periods only. The SelectionTab in Attribution renders UI controls for 1Y and SI (Since Inception), but the backend does not provide data for these periods. The Lambda must be updated to compute 1Y and SI attribution windows before these UI controls will function.

note.title: Valuation range drilldown: only 8 of 40+ indices have complete range data
note.description: The ValuationRangePanel (always visible, drilldown for a user-selected index) shows p10-p90 percentile range data. The yang-generate-valuation Lambda only produces ranges for 8 of the 40+ equity indices covered in the summary table. Indices without range data render a "pending" placeholder in the portal. Completing range coverage requires updating the Lambda to compute percentile thresholds for all indices.

note.title: PKL typo: "Kindom" should be "Kingdom" for MSCI entry
note.description: The data_pkl contains a spelling error in the MSCI Kingdom index name: stored as "Kindom" instead of "Kingdom". The portal works around this with a hardcoded constant mapping, but the underlying PKL source should be corrected to prevent future confusion and to avoid silent mismatches if the workaround is removed.

note.title: MOVE index data is null in yang-generate-volatility
note.description: The yang-generate-volatility Lambda fetches VIX data from FRED successfully, but MOVE (Merrill Lynch Option Volatility Estimate — bond market equivalent of VIX) data is currently null/empty. The Lambda structure supports MOVE but the data source is incomplete. The VolatilityTab's MOVE toggle will render with null/empty data until the MOVE data source in yang-generate-volatility is resolved.

note.title: Equity duration uses proxy value
note.description: portal/src/pages/Attribution/components/HoldingsTable.tsx hard-codes equity duration as a proxy value of 20.0 years. This is a display approximation, not derived from the yang pipeline output. Any accurate duration calculation would require Yang to include duration in the positioning_data.json or holdings_attribution_data.json response shape.

note.title: Factor key naming migration applied in portal constants
note.description: Factor key names were migrated in the portal to match the Yang PKL exactly: - 'Short vs Agg' renamed to 'Agg vs Short' - 'HY vs IG' renamed to 'HY vs Agg' The migration has been applied in portal/src/pages/FactorTilts/constants.ts (lines 16-17, 52-53). Any future changes to factor naming in the PKL must be synchronized with this constants file.

note.title: YieldCurveTab 1Y-ago curve requires separate FRED ingest
note.description: The YieldCurveTab displays a multi-snapshot USD Treasury yield curve (current, 1M-ago, 1Y-ago). The 1Y-ago snapshot requires running ingest_yield_curve_fred.py separately from the main yang pipeline. If this script has not been run, the 1Y-ago curve line will be absent or stale. This is an optional data enrichment, not a blocking dependency.

gap.description: This Lambda is included in the task order scope and is confirmed to exist at infra/aws/lambda/v2_portal/yang_pipeline/portfolios/yang-generate-peer-performance/. It produces json/peers/peer_performance.json containing peer universe percentile benchmarks for the 5 model portfolios across standard periods. However, the pod_inventory.xml for PortfolioAnalytics does not list a direct portal endpoint consuming peer_performance.json for any of the 6 pages in this pod. The peer performance data may be consumed by a different pod or by a future enhancement to the Attribution SelectionTab. Portal consumer mapping is unconfirmed.

The exact set of indicator slug names (used as S3 key suffixes in json/macro/timeseries/{slug}.json) could not be fully enumerated from static code analysis. The slugs are derived by slugifying the indicator display names from the data_pkl. The count is 44+ indicators. A complete slug list would require either running the Lambda or inspecting the PKL's macro indicator index. This gap means a DS cannot enumerate all available timeseries files without an execution-time reference.

The exact portal-proxy URL for yang-generate-volatility output (json/yang/volatility_data.json) could not be confirmed from static analysis of portal/src/api/portal-proxy.ts. The getVolatilityData() function exists (line 1637+) and is used by Macroeconomics.tsx, but whether it fetches from json/yang/volatility_data.json or json/macro/vix_data.json requires reading the full portal-proxy function body. Both files exist; the active path should be confirmed by reading portal-proxy.ts around line 1637.
